vignette: Kiet had always taken pride in his work as a plumber, able to fix any pipe or unclog any drain with ease. But since his captivity 10 years ago, he found himself avoiding jobs that required him to be alone with male clients. He would try to convince himself it was just a coincidence, but the truth was, being alone with men made him feel like he was back in that small, dingy room, with no escape. The memories of his captivity still haunted him, playing over and over in his mind like a film reel. He couldn't explain why, but certain dates and anniversaries connected to the event would send him into a tailspin, forcing him to detach himself from the memories altogether. He would try to occupy himself with work or TV, anything to distract himself from the replays of his time in captivity. But even at home, Kiet couldn't shake off the feeling of being on guard. He would find himself constantly scanning the room, looking for potential escape routes, just in case. His wife, Linh, had grown accustomed to this new behavior, but it still made her nervous. She would try to reassure him that everything was okay, but Kiet knew he wasn't being paranoid - not after what happened. Physical reactions were also a common occurrence for Kiet. Whenever something reminded him of the stressful experience, his body would react strongly. He would feel nauseous and his neck would ache, as if the memories themselves were causing physical pain. Even sudden movements by others could put him on high alert, making him jump or flinch. Kiet struggled to articulate what happened during his captivity. When he tried to explain it to Linh or their friends, he would lose his train of thought and struggle to find words. It was as if the memories were trapped inside him, unable to be verbalized. He knew what happened, but the words just wouldn't come. As a result, Kiet had become withdrawn, avoiding social gatherings and even simple errands. His plumbing business began to suffer, as he couldn't bear the thought of being alone with male clients or navigating unfamiliar spaces without an escape plan. Linh tried to be patient, but it was taking a toll on their relationship. One day, while working on a particularly difficult pipe, Kiet's neck pain flared up, and he felt a wave of nausea wash over him. He realized that he couldn't keep living like this - constantly on edge, unable to face his memories or share them with others. That was when he decided to seek help, hoping to find a way to break free from the grip of his captivity and regain control over his life. As Kiet sat in the therapist's office, he couldn't shake off the feeling that he was taking a risk by sharing his story. But something about being there, surrounded by calmness and understanding, made him feel like maybe, just maybe, he could finally start to heal. He looked up at the therapist, his eyes searching for reassurance, and began to speak - hesitantly at first, but with growing determination - of the memories that haunted him still.
